statusDetail: Atomic coverage complete across 58 checks and five representative public paths.

page.notes: Localized live-cam listing/detail application with age-verification, consent, login and app manifest. Cloudflare returns 403 to raw/crawler fetches.

artifacts.caption: Mobile entry page showing age and cookie banners
Mobile layout metrics and layout-shift/long-task observations
Metadata, semantics, forms, manifest and platform probe
Animation probe with reduced motion requested
Programmatic focus and target-size probe on login path
Live-room/detail archetype with age gate and chat
Compact trace timing and main-thread summary
Selected Lighthouse metrics and audit details
Heap after ten bottom/top scroll cycles

checkOutcomes.method: Emulated dark screenshot plus computed/CSS probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: The page remained the same hard-coded dark palette; colorScheme was normal and no prefers-color-scheme rules were found.

checkOutcomes.method: getAnimations under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce plus CSS rule scan
checkOutcomes.evidence: The reduce preference matched, yet two 250ms animations still ran and no reduced-motion media rule was found.
Lighthouse found multiple failures, including 2.55:1 banner copy, 2.74:1 highlighted text, and 3.7:1 cookie-accept text.

checkOutcomes.method: Rendered DOM/CSS feature probe across routes
checkOutcomes.evidence: The API exists in the browser, but no authored transition rules or transition treatment were observed across listing, room, login and 404 routes.

checkOutcomes.method: Recon across entry, listing, detail, login and 404 paths
checkOutcomes.evidence: No scroll-linked animation, parallax, scrollytelling, or entry/exit reveal was present on the representative pages.
checkOutcomes.reason: No scroll-linked animation, parallax, scrollytelling, or entry/exit reveal was present on the representative pages.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The listing uses native document scrolling without horizontal overflow or custom pointer gesture traps.
Headers/chrome remain static on long content and no scroll-state container-query treatment was found.

checkOutcomes.method: Recon across entry, listing, detail, login and 404 paths
checkOutcomes.evidence: No tooltip or edge-positioned popover was exposed in the representative public paths, so there was no anchored overlay to judge.
checkOutcomes.reason: No tooltip or edge-positioned popover was exposed in the representative public paths, so there was no anchored overlay to judge.

checkOutcomes.method: Visual review of navigation and recovery states
checkOutcomes.evidence: Selected tabs, room identity, headings and the 404 recovery CTA clearly communicate location and next action.
The cookie panel overlays the lower content while the age-verification banner occupies 136px near the top, leaving a constrained first viewport.

checkOutcomes.method: DOM primitive and semantic element counts
checkOutcomes.evidence: One dialog exists, but the persistent cookie overlay is custom page chrome rather than a native dismissible top-layer primitive.
Desktop devotes a persistent sidebar, two nav rows, age banner and cookie bar to chrome; mobile stacks two nav rows plus two overlays.
scrollWidth and clientWidth were both 360 with 0px horizontal overflow and a viewport meta tag.
No @container rules were found although cards/navigation are reused in materially different desktop and mobile containers.
Visible focused links reported outline-style none; many navigation links measured only 28px high.
The heading/content grid and room age-verification CTA make the browsing and viewing purpose explicit.
A listed performer opens into a room with visible age verification, public chat and clearly priced private/tip actions.
The room explains its gated state and the invalid route presents a localized 404 message plus a home-page recovery action.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse plus trace and layout primitives
checkOutcomes.evidence: Mobile Lighthouse measured LCP 15.8s and TBT 601ms; the first-party trace measured 400ms blocking, despite a 1.39s unthrottled LCP.
The layout primitive recorded CLS 0.1452 from a shift at about 2.47s; all 36 inspected images lacked width/height attributes.
The trace found four long tasks, longest 223ms, totaling 400ms blocking; Lighthouse TBT was 601ms.
The load made 161 requests and transferred 2.45MB; 36/36 images lacked dimensions, 15 below-fold images were not lazy, and 8 were oversized.
Lighthouse estimated 1,174,421 bytes of unused JavaScript while scripts accounted for 1.37MB transferred.

checkOutcomes.method: Rendered login DOM plus Lighthouse accessibility audit
checkOutcomes.evidence: The username and password inputs rely on placeholders and have neither associated labels nor aria-labels.
Lighthouse enumerated contrast failures in the age banner, footer, language control and cookie action.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse structure audit plus focus probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: Heading order had no reported violation, but the focus probe found visible interactive links with no focus outline.
Primary headings, card labels, room controls and 404 copy remain readable without clipping at representative sizes.
The viewport allows normal scaling, content reflows at 360px with no overflow, and Lighthouse reported no target-size failures.
Lighthouse reported no console-error items during the audited load.
DOCTYPE html and UTF-8 are correct, but every inspected image lacked explicit dimensions and 8 were more than 2x display size.
Lighthouse best-practices scored 0.58 and reported three deprecated API uses in the Cloudflare challenge script.
The page has a descriptive Spanish title and a 169-character meta description.
Raw fetch returned 403, only 2% of rendered content words survived, and title/H1/description were absent; direct robots and sitemap requests also received Cloudflare block pages.
The homepage declares a self-canonical, index/follow robots policy and 35 hreflang alternatives.
The page exposes one JSON-LD block and six Open Graph properties alongside matching visible content.
HTTPS and HSTS are present, but CSP and nosniff are absent and all 26 audited cookies were flagged insecure by the primitive, including 20+ without Secure.
The page contacted 10 third-party origins; assets.chapturist.com alone received 100 requests, before consent was accepted.
The public login flow offers password and passwordless options but no observed WebAuthn/passkey capability; no on-load permission request was observed.
HSTS and X-Frame-Options DENY are present, but CSP, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy and nosniff are missing.
A non-JS/raw client received HTTP 403 and only 2% rendered-content coverage; title, H1 and description did not survive.
The representative overlays and room controls remained within their viewports and loaded into stable, actionable states.
A manifest link exists, but the loaded page had no controlling service worker and no offline fallback was exposed.
The invalid route renders a localized 404, a clear explanation, a home CTA and alternative featured content.
html lang is es, Spanish UI is consistent, and 35 hreflang alternatives are declared; no RTL variant was in the selected locale.
Spanish copy, locale-domain routing and localized metadata are consistent; the public paths expose no hand-formatted currency/date strings requiring Intl verification.

checkOutcomes.method: Recon across entry, listing, detail, login and 404 paths
checkOutcomes.evidence: The audited public paths displayed no scheduled events, dates, or user-facing times that require time-zone or DST conversion.
checkOutcomes.reason: The audited public paths displayed no scheduled events, dates, or user-facing times that require time-zone or DST conversion.

checkOutcomes.method: Mobile consent screenshot and cookie audit
checkOutcomes.evidence: The green “Aceptar todas” button dominates while “Gestionar” is low-emphasis text; 26 cookies were already set before a consent choice.
The login inputs have no required attributes or accessible error linkage, and CAPTCHA prevented a meaningful native invalid-submit state.
Username and password inputs omit autocomplete=username and autocomplete=current-password, limiting safe password-manager/autofill assistance.
The gated room displays the private-show price (60 tokens) before action and makes age verification explicit; no subscription continuity was presented publicly.
15 images use legacy formats, 22 lack srcset, 8 are oversized and 15 below-fold images are not lazy-loaded.
The initial experience issues 161 requests, 51 XHR/fetches and four long main-thread tasks before user interaction.
Ten third-party origins participate in a 2.45MB initial load, with 100 requests to the asset host and 30 to an image CDN.

checkOutcomes.method: Recon across entry, listing, detail, login and 404 paths
checkOutcomes.evidence: Emerging capability judged out of scope: the public browsing and age-verification surfaces do not declare an agent-facing intent.
checkOutcomes.reason: Emerging capability judged out of scope: the public browsing and age-verification surfaces do not declare an agent-facing intent.

checkOutcomes.method: Recon across entry, listing, detail, login and 404 paths
checkOutcomes.evidence: No summarisation or language-model task is part of the representative user journeys, so on-device inference is not applicable.
checkOutcomes.reason: No summarisation or language-model task is part of the representative user journeys, so on-device inference is not applicable.

checkOutcomes.evidence: After ten bottom/top feed scroll cycles, node count grew 1,139,072→1,631,272 (+43%) and self size 54.1→75.4MB (+39%); dynamic feed loading makes leak confidence medium.
The initial page retained about 1.14M heap nodes and 54.1MB self size, high for a listing before user interaction.
Detached DOM constructors did not appear among the largest retained constructor populations in either summary; no direct listener accumulation was observed.

principleOutcomes.reason: Emerging capability judged out of scope: the public browsing and age-verification surfaces do not declare an agent-facing intent. No summarisation or language-model task is part of the representative user journeys, so on-device inference is not applicable.

paths.description: Homepage and primary discovery grid; represents entry, global navigation, notices and metadata.
Recommended listing; represents category/filter grid templates.
Performer room; represents live detail, age gate, chat and paid actions.
Authentication form; represents account entry and form semantics.
Invalid route; represents HTTP/navigation recovery state.

findings.summary: Several important controls and notices fail minimum contrast
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured ratios from 2.55:1 to 3.71:1 in the age banner, footer and cookie action.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust foreground/background tokens to at least WCAG AA and test all interactive states.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is not visibly exposed on many links
findings.evidence: Programmatically focused visible navigation links reported outline style none; many targets were only 28px high.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide a high-contrast :focus-visible ring and increase compact tap targets to at least 44 CSS px where practical.

findings.summary: Mobile loading and main-thread responsiveness are poor
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 15.8s and TBT 601ms; trace recorded four long tasks and 400ms blocking.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile LCP and long tasks, prioritize the hero/content request, and split/defer non-critical work.

findings.summary: The initial page ships a large, script-heavy dependency graph
findings.evidence: 161 requests transferred 2.45MB; JavaScript was 1.37MB and Lighthouse estimated 1.17MB unused.
findings.suggestedFix: Code-split by journey, remove duplicate/unused bundles, defer below-fold UI, and tighten caching/priorities.

findings.summary: Login fields lack durable labels and autofill semantics
findings.evidence: Rendered login HTML shows placeholder-only username/password fields with no labels, aria-labels or autocomplete tokens.
findings.suggestedFix: Add associated labels and autocomplete=username/current-password; keep placeholders as examples only.

findings.summary: Non-JavaScript crawlers receive a blocked shell
findings.evidence: Discoverability fetch returned 403 with 2% content coverage; title, H1 and description were absent, and robots/sitemap fetches hit Cloudflare blocks.
findings.suggestedFix: Allow verified crawlers to fetch server-rendered localized content and serve robots/sitemap without challenge.

findings.summary: Security headers and cookie flags are incomplete
findings.evidence: CSP, nosniff, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy are missing; 20+ first-party cookies lack Secure.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a nonce/hash CSP, nosniff, strict referrer/permissions policies, and Secure/SameSite cookie defaults.

findings.summary: A broad third-party footprint starts before consent
findings.evidence: Ten third-party origins load; one asset origin receives 100 requests and 26 cookies exist before consent acceptance.
findings.suggestedFix: Gate non-essential collection on consent, audit vendor purpose/retention, and consolidate/batch requests.

findings.summary: Consent presentation favors acceptance after collection has begun
findings.evidence: “Aceptar todas” is the dominant green button, “Gestionar” is subdued text, and 26 cookies were already present.
findings.suggestedFix: Give accept/reject/manage equal prominence and delay non-essential storage/network activity until an informed choice.

findings.summary: Network and background work are disproportionate before interaction
findings.evidence: The initial load performs 161 requests, 51 fetch/XHR calls, 10 third-party origins and four long tasks.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a route budget, defer non-visible feeds/media, pause background work offscreen, and remove low-value third parties.

findings.summary: Theme ignores the user color-scheme preference
findings.evidence: Dark emulation produced the same hard-coded dark UI; computed color-scheme is normal and CSS probe found no preference rules.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and use prefers-color-scheme/light-dark() to provide user-driven light and dark palettes.

findings.summary: Reduced-motion preference is not implemented
findings.evidence: With reduce matched, two 250ms animations still ran and no reduced-motion rule was found.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a prefers-reduced-motion: reduce layer that removes non-essential transitions and auto-motion.

findings.summary: Stacked age and cookie notices constrain the first mobile viewport
findings.evidence: At 360x800, fixed cookie chrome covers the lower cards while the age banner occupies the top 136px.
findings.suggestedFix: Consolidate notices, reserve layout space, and use a semantic dismissible surface without obscuring core cards.

findings.summary: Navigation and persistent notices dominate the content frame
findings.evidence: Desktop stacks sidebar, dual nav, age banner and cookie bar; mobile stacks dual nav and two notices.
findings.suggestedFix: Progressively disclose secondary navigation and compact chrome once users begin scrolling.

findings.summary: Late content causes excessive layout shift
findings.evidence: Mobile layout observer recorded CLS 0.1452 and the image audit found no explicit dimensions on 36 images.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve image/banner geometry with width, height or aspect-ratio and stabilize late notice insertion.

findings.summary: Image delivery is unstable and wasteful
findings.evidence: All 36 images lacked dimensions; 22 lacked srcset, 15 were legacy format, 15 below-fold were eager, and 8 were oversized.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit width/height, responsive srcset/sizes, modern formats and lazy loading for below-fold media.

findings.summary: Authentication does not expose phishing-resistant passkeys
findings.evidence: The login UI offers password and passwordless entry but no observed WebAuthn/passkey path.
findings.suggestedFix: Add passkey registration/authentication and retain passwordless fallback; request permissions only in context.

findings.summary: The app-like experience has no controlling service worker
findings.evidence: A manifest is declared, but the page had no service-worker controller or offline fallback.
findings.suggestedFix: Add an offline shell/fallback and cache resilient static/navigation resources appropriate to the live product.

findings.summary: Login error semantics are not evident
findings.evidence: Login inputs omit required and accessible error-linkage attributes; CAPTCHA blocks submission before a useful field-error state.
findings.suggestedFix: Validate after interaction and synchronize :user-invalid, aria-invalid, described errors and an aria-live summary.

findings.summary: The feed retains a large and growing heap footprint
findings.evidence: Baseline was 1.14M nodes/54.1MB; after ten scroll cycles it was 1.63M/75.4MB. Infinite-feed loading lowers leak certainty but the growth is material.
findings.suggestedFix: Repeat in one instrumented session with GC checkpoints, then virtualize cards and release stale objects/listeners when evidence confirms retention.

findings.summary: Route changes have no authored transition treatment
findings.evidence: The API is available, but route review and CSS inspection found no view-transition rules.
findings.suggestedFix: Use same-document or cross-document View Transitions for listing/detail and recovery navigation, with reduced-motion fallback.

findings.summary: Long-page chrome does not respond to scroll state
findings.evidence: The long listing retains static stacked chrome and no scroll-state rules were found.
findings.suggestedFix: Use scroll-state container queries to compact persistent headers and preserve content space after scrolling.

findings.summary: Reusable cards and navigation do not use container-aware adaptation
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found zero @container rules across components shown in very different desktop/mobile containers.
findings.suggestedFix: Add container-type to reusable regions and size-aware component rules, retaining viewport fallbacks.

findings.summary: A challenge dependency uses deprecated browser APIs
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported three deprecated API uses in the Cloudflare challenge script and best-practices scored 0.58.
findings.suggestedFix: Update/configure the challenge integration and monitor DevTools deprecation reports.
